analysis: Changed behavior is small. (1) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 adds superviseServingAuthorization() to capacityRefreshTick, run on the capacity cadence before writeDaemonState(). (2) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift adds noteCoordinatorConnection(connected:) at startup (after logger.info(.coordinatorClientStarted), head ~line 293), in the event-reader switch for .connected/.disconnected (head ~419, using event.isConnected), and after the event stream ends (head ~429), directly before clearConnectionAuthorization() and cancelAppAttestShadow(). In every case the existing invalidation calls still run; the new call only records connection state, so nothing in the diff removes or reorders authorization clearing. The bodies of noteCoordinatorConnection, superviseServingAuthorization and CoordinatorEvent.isConnected are not in the supplied evidence. Neither is the supervision policy, such as expiry or stall handling. I cannot confirm that supervision never extends or re-grants authorization (T-053, T-057, A-016), that it cannot block the actor, or that it does not write sensitive data via writeDaemonState (T-058). No visible regression: the call is synchronous, and the tick already invokes similar synchronous and awaited supervisors. The T-041 prefix-cache telemetry paths in updateAggregateCapacity are unchanged context. Next review should inspect the implementations of noteCoordinatorConnection and superviseServingAuthorization (likely in another file of this PR), checking that: expiry and revocation are fail-closed; the 'connected: false' initial state at startup cannot leave stale authorization valid; no race exists between the reader task (eventTask) and work FIFO ordering; and the supervision does not log grant identifiers.
